references.text: Matthew's parallel account of the healing of Peter's mother-in-law, where Jesus entered Peter's house and saw his mother-in-law lying sick with a fever.

Mark's parallel account of the healing of Simon's mother-in-law. Jesus left the synagogue and went directly into the house of Simon and Andrew, where Simon's mother-in-law was lying sick with a fever.
The preceding context in Luke where Jesus teaches in the synagogue in Capernaum, explaining that he now leaves the synagogue and goes to Simon's house.
Simon Peter is introduced by his brother Andrew and given the name Cephas by Jesus, showing the relationship between Jesus and Simon as background for why Jesus visits Simon's home.
Luke's account of the calling of Simon Peter, which follows shortly after the healing of his mother-in-law, and shows the growing relationship between Jesus and Simon.
Paul mentions that Cephas (Peter) had a wife, which aligns with Peter having a mother-in-law as mentioned here.
A similar pattern where some ask Jesus for help on behalf of a sick person, just as the disciples here asked Jesus to help Simon's mother-in-law.
